title: Put first-aid supplies within wheelchair reach
instruction: Put the first-aid kit and the bandages where a wheelchair user can reach them, as the ADA accessibility standards define it. The wall and its ledges are at 1:10 scale.
context: The 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design set the range a seated person can reach: where a forward reach is unobstructed, the high reach is 48 inches (1220 mm) maximum and the low reach 15 inches (380 mm) minimum above the floor (section 308.2.1); a side reach from a parallel approach has the same limits (308.3.1). Storage elements must meet one of those ranges (811.3), and where storage is provided in accessible spaces at least one of each type must (225.2). The instruction names the standard, not the heights, and one item starts too high and the other too low. Done by: nursing assistants and facilities staff.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. In front of the right arm, a fixed cream wall (20 mm thick, 340 mm wide, 140 mm tall, 1.4 m at 1:10) has its face 33.5 cm out from the bases. Three fixed brown ledges, 60 mm deep and 6 mm thick, stick out from it side by side, none above another: the high ledge (60 mm wide, top 135 mm above the table) 1.5 cm in from the right arm's base, the middle ledge (140 mm wide, top 80 mm) 13.5 cm in, and the low ledge (60 mm wide, top 12 mm) 3 cm right of the midline. A green first-aid kit (24 x 30 x 22 mm, 50 g) sits on the high ledge and a blue box of bandages (24 x 26 x 22 mm, 50 g) on the low ledge, each centred 35 mm out from the wall.
scoring: An item is within reach when the whole of it is 15 to 48 in above the floor at scale (38 to 122 mm above the table, which stands for the floor), it stands on a ledge or on the other item (bottom within 2 mm, not held in the air), and it lies on any face within 10 degrees of flat. 0.5 for each item within reach; 1.0 when both are and both are still for 1 s, which ends the trial. Both items start out of range: the kit on the high ledge spans 53 to 62 in, the bandages on the low ledge 5 to 13 in. Only the middle ledge (31.5 to 40 in for an item standing on it) is in range.
reset_notes: Put the first-aid kit back on the high ledge and the bandages on the low ledge.
fidelity: The wall and ledges are at 1:10, and so are the kit and the bandage box (a 24 x 30 cm kit). The table stands for the floor. The whole item must be in range, so it doesn't matter which part a person reaches for. The wall, ledges and items have rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
